question: A 19-year-old man consulted for a 24-hour history of pain, swelling and functional impotence of the right knee accompanied by a fever of 38ºC. Physical examination reveals inflammatory signs and joint effusion in the right knee. The analytical data show a leukocytosis with neutrophilia and an elevation of the C-reactive protein. The syndromic diagnosis of acute monoarthritis is made. What is the most likely etiologic diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "19-year-old man with knee pain" -> "24-hour history of symptoms" -> "fever of 38ºC" -> "inflammatory signs and joint effusion" -> "leukocytosis with neutrophilia" -> "elevated C-reactive protein" -> "acute monoarthritis diagnosis" -> "most likely due to bacterial infection" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Acute monoarthritis presentation" -> "fever and joint effusion" -> "leukocytosis with neutrophilia" -> "elevated C-reactive protein" -> "suggestive of infection" -> "bacterial infectious arthritis is common in young adults" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Joint effusion and fever" -> "inflammatory response indicated" -> "neutrophilia present" -> "bacterial infection likely" -> "other causes less probable" -> "reactive arthritis less likely due to absence of preceding infection" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Knee pain with fever and swelling" -> "acute inflammatory signs" -> "high leukocyte count" -> "C-reactive protein elevation" -> "bacterial infectious arthritis is a common cause" -> "mycobacterial infection less likely in this age group" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Acute monoarthritis in young male" -> "fever and leukocytosis" -> "neutrophilia suggests infection" -> "bacterial infectious arthritis is a leading cause" -> "other options less likely" -> 88%
analysis: The clinical presentation of acute monoarthritis in a young man, characterized by pain, swelling, fever, leukocytosis with neutrophilia, and elevated C-reactive protein, strongly suggests an infectious etiology. The rapid onset and inflammatory signs point towards bacterial infectious arthritis as the most likely cause, especially given the acute nature of the symptoms. Other options such as microcrystal arthritis, reactive arthritis, mycobacterial infection, and rheumatoid arthritis are less likely given the acute presentation and the patient's age.
